The owl watching your AI team — spend, AI work time, and memory per employee, in your terminal and macOS menu bar.

Exe Watcher shows what your AI coding work costs, how long the agents run, and how each Exe OS employee's memory grows. Track nine coding clients, models, projects, tokens, and optimization findings from local usage files. Spend and time tracking need no API keys, account, proxy, or wrappers around your tools; employee memory and spend appear when Exe OS supplies its local agent stats. **Forked from [CodeBurn by AgentSeal](https://github.com/getagentseal/codeburn) on April 24, 2026.** Since then, Exe AI has developed Watcher for AI employee teams and parallel agent workflows. [Development timeline and comparison](#development-since-the-codeburn-fork) · [Origin and MIT attribution](#origin--attribution) **macOS app:** Download the universal DMG from [Releases](https://github.com/AskExe/exe-watcher/releases/latest), drag **Watcher by EXE** into **Applications**, and open it. macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon or Intel. From 0.2.55, Node and the CLI are included. **Terminal CLI** (Node 22.13+): Node 23.0–23.3 require an upgrade to 23.4 or newer; SQLite is unavailable by default on those older versions. ```bash npm install -g exe-watcher exe-watcher report ``` Version 0.2.70 adds local active AI app tracking and broader, clearly labeled historical personal-time estimates. It also explains that first-time history setup can take 10 minutes or more for large AI histories, with saved progress and recovery details. Large Claude history scans resume within the existing resource limits. Recorded API-equivalent costs and saved totals are preserved through refresh failures, restarts and day changes. AI time and the floating quota display are included. Terminal installs require Node 22.13 or newer; the Mac app includes its own compatible runtime. Download the matching app from [Releases](https://github.com/AskExe/exe-watcher/releases/latest) or [odd.community/watcher](https://odd.community/watcher). To run the current CLI from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/AskExe/exe-watcher.git cd exe-watcher npm ci npm run build node dist/cli.js report ``` --- ## Built for AI employee teams - **Floating display** — a compact on-screen quota display for Claude, Codex, Kimi, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Gemini, with **You + AI ≈** (historical sessions plus tracked app activity) and **AI Time** (work time added across all agents). Quota rings show **quota left**, default to **Weekly**, and have a **Weekly / 5h** toggle. Click either time button for its explanation. Time totals default to Today; switch to Week, Month or All Time. Enable it from the menu bar footer’s **Display settings → Floating quota display**. [Details](mac/README.md#floating-display). - **AI running time** — adds recorded work across agents, so parallel work is counted as agent-hours. - **Elapsed busy time** — merges overlapping runs to show how long at least one agent was working. - **Your time ≈** — estimates interaction from short reply-to-next-prompt gaps, with known subagents excluded. It is not an attention or productivity measurement. - **Memory per employee** — shows persistent memory counts and growth over 24 hours, 7 days, and 30 days from Exe OS. These are saved memories, not RAM usage. - **Spend per employee** — puts model-aware 24-hour, 7-day, and 30-day cost beside the same Exe OS employee identities. - **Bounded background work** — coalesces usage-file events, reuses cached periods, resumes historical recovery, and rests between scans. - **Visible data limits** — distinguishes unknown timing, missing historical call counts, recovered usage, and models whose costs cannot be priced. - **One local view** — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cursor Agent, Copilot, OpenCode, Kimi Code, OMP, and Pi, with no usage-data upload service. ## Development since the CodeBurn fork Watcher started as an import of CodeBurn 0.8.9 on **April 24, 2026**. By this review on **October 16, 2026**, it had **175 days of independent development—nearly six months**. | Date (2026) | Watcher development milestone | | --- | --- | | April 24 | Imported the CodeBurn foundation and began the Exe rebrand as exe-fuelbar. | | April 27–28 | Added Exe OS memory integration and the AI Employees section with per-agent memory growth and spend. | | April 30 | Renamed the product to Watcher. | | May–June | Improved accounting, period consistency, wake/recovery behavior, provider isolation, and model presentation. | | October 3 | Added bounded event-driven usage refreshes, retained-history recovery, and pricing/accounting corrections. | | October 14–15 | Added self-contained universal macOS packaging, the chosen owl artwork and animation, native Kimi usage, and clearer historical call coverage. | | October 16 | Added the three AI time totals, provider coverage, a resumable timing index, automatic timing catch-up, and the floating quota/time display. | ### Where Watcher differs today Comparison checked against [CodeBurn 0.9.27, revision 9a40cc6](https://github.com/getagentseal/codeburn/tree/9a40cc603fcd194caca9daa8c5134a61ea7e0e2b) on October 16, 2026. | Capability | Watcher | CodeBurn at the reviewed revision | | --- | --- | --- | | Three separate time totals across supported clients | AI running, overlap-adjusted elapsed busy, and estimated interaction time, filtered by period/provider/project | Session-duration and Codex generation-timing metrics exist; no equivalent three-total report was found. | | Persistent memory per AI employee | Exe OS memory count plus 24h / 7d / 30d growth | No equivalent employee-memory ledger was found. | | Exe OS employee integration | Memory and spend use Exe OS employee IDs and local daemon stats; includes agent-pipeline diagnostics | Agent/subagent spend views exist; no Exe OS employee/stats integration was found. | Our subsequent work also includes accounting fixes, bounded history recovery, event-driven native refreshes, current API pricing, Kimi support, self-contained packaging, and Watcher's visual identity. These are documented improvements to our imported baseline; some capabilities also exist in today's CodeBurn. [Detailed evidence and adoption backlog](docs/codeburn-upstream-review.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) Watcher’s floating display takes inspiration from CodeBurn’s **Capacity Dock** and adds our two time totals. It supports six quota providers, including Claude and Codex, with Weekly as their default and a 5-hour toggle. OS threshold notifications and additional adapters remain in the [adoption backlog](docs/codeburn-upstream-review.md). --- ## Features ### Native macOS menu bar app ```bash exe-watcher menubar # install + launch exe-watcher menubar --force # reinstall latest exe-watcher menubar --version v0.2.60 # install a specific version exe-watcher # on macOS: prompts to install menubar app ``` > **Note:** Running `exe-watcher` with no subcommand on macOS prompts you to install the menubar app. In non-interactive environments (pipes, CI), it shows help instead. Use `exe-watcher --help` to see all available commands. A Swift/SwiftUI popover that lives in your menu bar. Today's spend is always visible at a glance. - **Period switcher** — Today, 7 Days, 30 Days, Month, All Time. Each period includes comparison to the previous window where available. - **Provider tabs** — Switch between All, Claude, Codex, Cursor, and any other detected provider with spend. - **Insight tabs** — Trend, Forecast, Pulse, and Stats summarize token/cost movement, projections, optimization wins, and usage streaks. - **Activity breakdown** — Research, Building, Debugging, DevOps, Testing, and Planning with cost, turns, and one-shot rate. - **Model breakdown** — See which models are driving spend and call volume. - **Project spend** — Per-project cost across today / 7d / 30d. - **AI time** — AI running, elapsed busy, and estimated interaction time for the selected period, with timing coverage details. - **AI Employees** — Exe OS memory growth and employee spend, when local daemon data is available. - **Optimization findings** — Menubar links open the full optimizer or report directly in Terminal. - **Plan budgets** — Compare API-equivalent spend with built-in monthly budget presets or a custom budget. - **Live Claude capacity** — Five-hour and weekly utilization, reset times, and projections from the signed-in Claude account. This optional view uses provider credentials and may request macOS Keychain access. - **Capacity estimation** — Derives likely token limits from usage patterns when hard caps aren't published. - **Multi-currency** — USD, GBP, EUR, JPY, AUD, CAD, CHF, CNY, SEK, NOK, DKK, NZD, SGD, HKD, KRW, INR, BRL. - **Animated owl** — Glances and blinks while the popover is visible, with Reduce Motion support. macOS pushes usage-log change notifications to Watcher; there is no repeating background usage scan. Rapid writes are combined, with at least two minutes of rest after a scan and longer after slow scans (nine times the scan duration). A failed notification gets at most two spaced retries before waiting for new data or a user action. Watcher also catches up on launch/wake and explicit user actions. Only one CLI child runs at a time, at low scheduling priority, with a 256 MiB V8 heap limit and a 60-second timeout. Historical and provider detail views load on demand. Failed scans retain the last successful total, including across app restarts on the same date; missing data after midnight displays a dash until a scan succeeds. ### AI time The menu bar dashboard and full terminal report show three times beneath the spending overview. They follow the selected day, 7 days, 30 days, month or all-time view, with the same provider and project filters: - **AI running:** recorded run time added across agents. Two agents running for one hour add two hours. Duplicate run IDs copied into forks count once. - **Elapsed busy:** time when at least one agent was running. Those two parallel agents count as one elapsed hour. - **Your time ≈:** historical conversation sessions plus foreground app activity tracked on this Mac. Historical sessions join nearby main-chat turn starts with a 15-minute gap; the displayed sensitivity range uses 10–30 minutes. It includes some AI waiting, excludes known subagents and long unattended gaps, and may include main-chat automation. Isolated turns get no invented padding. This is an estimate of engagement, not attention or typing. The older five-minute reply-gap estimate remains available in JSON as `userActiveMs` and in CLI details. **Track active AI app time on this Mac** can be switched off in the AI time section. It counts foreground Codex, Hansel, Claude and ChatGPT app activity, with a two-minute idle cutoff. Cursor, supported editors and terminals count only alongside a recent matching AI turn; these ambiguous intervals are marked as contextual estimates. Browsers and unsupported apps remain unknown. No keyboard contents, window titles, screenshots, accessibility access or Terminal control are needed. App switching, sleep and console-session notifications drive tracking; a single 30-second idle check runs only while an eligible app is in front. Late checks never fill sleep or scheduler gaps. Daily totals are saved privately, at most every five minutes while continuously active and on app switch/exit; a crash can lose the unsaved tail. No usage scan or extra CLI process is triggered. A writer lock prevents two Watcher copies counting the same foreground activity. The historical estimate stops when app tracking first begins, so it is never added over the same time as app activity. Period and provider views use the same boundaries. App tracking gaps while Watcher is closed or tracking is off stay unknown. Daily app totals have no project attribution; project-filtered CLI reports show historical sessions only. The stored tracking timezone is fixed to avoid overlapping days after travel. Custom partial-day CLI queries omit daily app totals they cannot precisely locate. Timing recovery starts July 1, 2025 and uses retained local evidence. **Partial history** stays visible; missing timing is **Unknown**, never zero. Recorded durations may include tool execution and waiting, rather than only time generating tokens. Open runs are not extended to the present. | Client | Available timing evidence | |--------|---------------------------| | Claude Code | Recorded turn durations; older prompt/reply clocks are inferred | | Codex | Completed/interrupted run boundaries or durations; older reply clocks are inferred | | Cursor IDE | Saved conversation message start/end clocks, when retained | | Cursor Agent | Timestamped CLI result durations; ordinary text transcripts lack clocks | | Copilot | Saved assistant turn start/end pairs | | OpenCode | Completed message clocks, including archived sessions and subagents; late/missing completions use short inferred spans from saved parts | | Kimi Code | Native saved step boundaries, including separate agents | | Pi / OMP | Inferred prompt-to-final-reply spans | Inferred spans are capped at 30 minutes; longer unmeasured gaps remain unknown. Deleted logs, unsupported formats and sessions without complete clocks cannot supply a full lifetime total. Provider details show how many files have usable timing in the selected period. Timing uses a separate private index and leaves financial history intact. Existing usage-file events trigger small bounded updates; no extra polling service is installed. Historical recovery advances saved byte cursors in bounded passes, without rereading unchanged transcripts. The menu bar continues known unfinished timing work in separate timing-only steps, without waiting for another file change or rerunning cost scans. Only one CLI child runs at a time; each step rests for at least nine times its elapsed runtime. Catch-up stops when the queue clears, an incomplete final record needs more data, a step fails, or two steps make no progress. Cost freshness timestamps stay unchanged. Provider file counts mean files with timing **in the selected view**, out of all discovered files. ```bash exe-watcher time --period all # saved/recent timing and coverage exe-watcher time --period week --format json exe-watcher time --recover --period all # one bounded historical pass ``` Repeat a recovery pass while files remain pending and progress advances. Automatic parsing is capped at 16 MiB per update; explicit historical parsing at 256 MiB per pass. Incomplete or unreadable records remain clearly marked. ### Memory and spend per AI employee When [Exe OS](https://github.com/AskExe/exe-os) supplies local agent stats, Watcher adds an **AI Employees** section to the menu bar with two panels: - **Memory** — Persistent memory count for each employee, with 24h / 7d / 30d growth columns. This tracks saved knowledge records, not runtime memory consumption or memory quality. - **Employee Spend** — Per-employee cost across 24h / 7d / 30d, using the model-aware cost buckets supplied by Exe OS. How it works: 1. Exe OS maps Claude Code sessions to employee I …[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]… rs, and recorded web search costs. Claude streaming records are reconciled by API message ID using cumulative token counters; final usage is counted once. Counted usage keeps its recorded API-equivalent dollar amount. Pricing refreshes apply to newly counted usage and never trigger an automatic repricing of saved history. Committed daily totals remain cached; new dates and missing providers add usage on top. A small local ledger retains hashed usage identities and their dollar amounts independently of temporary parsing caches, so unchanged accounting stays fixed even after cache eviction or a session append. New or corrected accounting records are new data. JSON reports include `pricing` metadata with this recorded-rates basis, the current feed refresh timestamp and source URLs. These are estimates, not historical invoices. Recovered history with missing request details remains an estimate. Models without published token prices (including Codex Spark) retain their tokens and an explicit cost-exclusion warning; an unknown price is not a final zero-dollar value. Switching Claude accounts does not filter usage: Watcher counts all retained sessions in the configured data directory and Claude Desktop account folders. Codex archived sessions also count. Add other Claude profile roots with `claudeConfigDirs` in `~/.config/exe-watcher/config.json`. “All Time” includes the entire available history. To set the beginning of your coding journey, add `"historyStartDate": "2025-07-01"` to the same config. This defines the reporting window; it cannot recreate missing logs. Unknown model prices generate a warning while their tokens remain counted. For unfiltered All Time Claude totals, Watcher also reconciles `stats-cache.json` cumulative model counters with retained logs through the snapshot's cutoff date. Only missing per-model/token counters are added. Recovered usage is separately identified as `historicalRecovery`: it has no fabricated dates, sessions, or projects, and uses standard API rates with 5-minute cache writes because TTL/speed metadata is unavailable. Daily charts show dated logs only. Project/provider sums include recovery only where attribution is known. Usage lost from both logs and cumulative counters remains unknown. These are API-equivalent estimates, not subscription charges or invoices. **Environment variables:** | Variable | Description | |----------|-------------| | `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | Override Claude data directory (default: `~/.claude`) | | `CODEX_HOME` | Override Codex data directory (default: `~/.codex`) | | `KIMI_CODE_HOME` | Override native Kimi Code data directory (default: `~/.kimi-code`) | | `XDG_DATA_HOME` | Base data directory for OpenCode (default: `~/.local/share`) | | `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Base directory for Watcher configuration (default: `~/.config`) | | `EXE_WATCHER_CACHE_DIR` | Override cache directory (default: `~/.cache/exe-watcher`) | ### Optional analytics and error reporting Watcher uses our self-hosted PostHog and Sentry through `https://data.odd.community`. Basic usage statistics default on after a first-run disclosure. Sanitized error diagnostics are a separate, optional choice and default off. Existing opt-outs are preserved. In the Mac app, find both controls under the Settings gear. In the CLI: ```sh exe-watcher telemetry --usage on --errors on exe-watcher telemetry --usage off --errors off ``` Usage counts participating installations, foreground feature use, active Mac menu time, and fixed success/failure outcomes, with numeric app version and coarse platform metadata. Recording time is N/A. Errors include only category, class and app version. No prompts, usage logs, project names, paths, spend, raw error text, native crash dumps, screenshots or replay are sent. Background CLI scans do not count as use. `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` or `EXE_WATCHER_TELEMETRY=0` disables collection. Turning a control off clears its unsent queue; received reports remain. Our collector receives your connection IP but does not forward it to PostHog/Sentry. No project keys are needed. See [privacy, retry behavior and operator setup](docs/analytics/README.md). --- ## Contributing Contributions welcome. The provider plugin system is the easiest entry point — each provider is a single file in `src/providers/`. ``` src/ cli.ts Entry point (Commander.js) dashboard.tsx TUI (Ink — React for terminals) parser.ts Session reader, dedup, date filter models.ts Pricing catalog and verified model aliases official-pricing.ts Official provider pricing overrides classifier.ts Activity classifier (6 categories) compare-stats.ts Model comparison engine menubar-json.ts Menu bar payload, employee stats and project spend resource-budget.ts Scan memory, runtime and output limits history-build.ts Resumable historical accounting time-tracking.ts AI running, elapsed busy and interaction estimates time-index.ts Separate bounded timing index and recovery export.ts CSV/JSON export config.ts Config management currency.ts Currency conversion providers/ One file per supported tool mac/ Native macOS menubar app (Swift + SwiftUI) tests/ CLI data integrity tests (Vitest) ``` --- ## Origin & attribution Watcher is an independently developed derivative of [CodeBurn](https://github.com/getagentseal/codeburn) by [AgentSeal](https://github.com/getagentseal), used under the MIT license. It began as a source import into a new repository on **April 24, 2026 at 14:40 Asia/Makassar (06:40 UTC)**, initially named exe-fuelbar. It is a fork in the development sense; GitHub does not list this repository as a fork. The [initial import](https://github.com/AskExe/exe-watcher/commit/8545e35633958ab3fd12600c1ac89c528c867904) contains 112 files identical to the corresponding files in [CodeBurn commit d3c4de0](https://github.com/getagentseal/codeburn/commit/d3c4de03759f0ded38052874fa829709d27fe7c6), whose package version was 0.8.9. These were already present at import and belong in CodeBurn's credit. **Watcher's subsequent work** includes its Exe branding and owl artwork, Exe OS agent/memory integration, bounded event-driven refreshes and history recovery, accounting and pricing corrections, native Kimi Code support, self-contained macOS packaging, and AI running/elapsed/interaction time reporting. The roadmap serves our AI employee teams and multi-agent workflows. # Shared private PostHog + Sentry integration

Use **`@odd-core/analytics/privacy`** for Odd's self-hosted counter/error collector.
It is separate from the older generic API at `@odd-core/analytics` and from
`@odd-core/telemetry`; those APIs do not enforce this wire protocol or its defaults.
The privacy entry point has no runtime dependencies or provider SDKs. Its source
and the matching Node gateway are MIT licensed. This change does not publish npm
artifacts or make the containing repository public.

## New app setup

1. Create separate PostHog and Sentry projects for the app. A CLI and a native app
   may use separate Sentry projects/aliases. Reuse the existing **build-my** server.
2. Register public aliases, the app slug, and static feature/source allowlists in
   the gateway's private maps (see below). Never copy Hansel's project IDs/aliases.
3. Install/link `@odd-core/analytics` through the app's normal dependency process.
   Build it with `tsc -b packages/types packages/analytics` from this repository.
   In this workspace, use `"@odd-core/analytics": "workspace:*"`.
4. Supply private storage and a cryptographic UUID provider, then expose **two
   independent opt-in controls**, both initially off. Keys/configuration alone
   never constitute consent. Update the app's privacy policy/store disclosures.
5. Hook explicit features, foreground/idle state, real recording completion, and
   handled structural errors to the client. Schedule `flush()` on a bounded timer
   and lifecycle transitions. No timers or error hooks start automatically.
6. Verify real local app usage and one harmless handled error in the app's own
   dashboards. Check opt-out, no pre-consent history, retry IDs, and tenant routing
   before the app's normal release process. No paid/cloud build is required here.

```ts
import { ActiveClock, PrivacyClient } from '@odd-core/analytics/privacy';

const analytics = await PrivacyClient.create({
  app: 'watcher',
  usageAlias: 'public-watcher-v1',       // provision first; illustrative values
  diagnosticsAlias: 'public-watcher-cli-v1',
  features: ['home', 'menu'],           // static developer-owned list, not user text
  storage: privateAppStorage,          // getItem/setItem, atomic durable replacement
  randomUUID: () => crypto.randomUUID(),
  // collector defaults to https://data.odd.community
});

// Only after the user accepts the relevant disclosure:
await analytics.setConsent({ usage: true });
await analytics.track({ event: 'active' }); // startup/return-to-active, not background polls
await analytics.track({ event: 'feature', feature: 'menu' });

const clock = new ActiveClock();
// Sample about every 5 seconds using a monotonic clock and actual app state.
// Skip/reset the clock while consent is off, after consent changes, and on sleep.
if (analytics.status().usage) {
  const active_ms = clock.sample(performance.now(), isFocused, idleSeconds, isRecording);
  if (active_ms > 0) await analytics.track({ event: 'usage', active_ms });
} else clock.reset();

// Recording apps only: duration from the actual completed recording, no audio/text.
await analytics.track({ event: 'recording', recording_ms: 3700 });

// Separate diagnostics consent, followed by a safe structural report.
await analytics.setConsent({ diagnostics: true });
await analytics.report({ event: 'error', category: 'ipc_error',
  error_class: 'RangeError', version: '1.0.0', frames: [] });
await analytics.flush();

// On revocation: abort pending requests, erase the channel queue and usage ID.
await analytics.setConsent({ usage: false });
clock.reset();
```

`setConsent`, `track`, and `report` return a boolean: check it when displaying
settings or troubleshooting persistence. A storage failure disables both channels
in memory. If a revocation cannot be persisted, the app must keep collection off
on subsequent launches until it can durably save the choice. One client instance
owns each app state store; don't share a writable queue across processes/tabs.
Already accepted server events cannot be recalled by aborting a request.

## Platform adapters

| Platform | Adapter responsibilities |
| --- | --- |
| Node CLI / Electron main | Owner-only atomic file replacement (directory `0700`, files `0600`), `node:crypto.randomUUID`, explicit lifecycle flush. Renderer requests cross a narrow, validated IPC boundary. Suppress background child CLI polling. |
| Web | App-scoped storage, Web Crypto UUIDs, visibility/focus/idle sampling. Configure exact CORS origins on the gateway and ingress. Cross-origin cookies are omitted. Browser storage is accessible to same-origin code. |
| React Native / Expo | Durable app-scoped storage, platform cryptographic UUIDs, foreground state and actual activity/idle signals. Keep Node modules out of the mobile bundle. |
| Native Swift/Kotlin/Dart | Implement the small protocol below or bridge this client; JavaScript cannot be imported directly into Swift. Reuse the same consent/storage/lifecycle rules and gateway allowlists. |

Never install global native crash handlers or send minidumps/raw crash reports as
part of this kit. Sentry gets explicit sanitized structural errors. There are no
automatic breadcrumbs, network traces, replay, screenshots, account identification,
device fingerprints, prompt/transcript/audio collection, or Google analytics.
DAU counts consenting installations, not authenticated people. Recording minutes
are **N/A** for apps without a recording feature. Metric days are UTC in the pilot.
IP addresses necessarily reach the collection network edge; the gateway does not
forward incoming IP/user-agent/cookies to PostHog or Sentry. Edge logging and
retention are operator responsibilities; pseudonymous analytics is still data.

## Persistence and transport contract

Both queues are capped at **500 events**, expire after **7 days**, and are
re-sanitized on load. UUID/timestamp are assigned once before retries, preserving
the backend deduplication key. Each flush sends at most 50 usage and 10 errors,
with 5s/10s timeouts. Failures retain safe events for the next scheduled attempt.
Re-enabling usage after revocation creates a fresh random installation UUID.
The state is bound to collector/app/aliases so a config change cannot reroute an
old queue. App adapters must not backfill history or generate synthetic activity.

`POST /batch/`, JSON content type:

```json
{"api_key":"public-watcher-v1","batch":[{
  "uuid":"a1c01189-72bf-4f63-b6e6-9e940e87ebc7","timestamp":"2026-10-23T12:00:00.000Z",
  "event":"app_feature","properties":{
    "distinct_id":"a1c01189-72bf-4f63-b6e6-9e940e87ebc8","app":"watcher","feature":"menu"
  }
}]}
```

Usage events: `app_active` (no counter), `app_usage` (`active_ms`, integer 1–60000),
`app_recording` (`recording_ms`, integer 1–86400000), `app_feature` (registered enum).
`POST /errors/`: same envelope/UUID/timestamp but each row has `diagnostic` instead
of `event`/`properties`. Diagnostic fields: `event: "error"`, fixed `category`,
standard JS `error_class` (unknown becomes `Error`), numeric `x.y.z` version, and
up to 8 registered logical frames with bounded integer line/column numbers.
Never put a raw exception object, message, stack string, arbitrary properties,
filesystem path, attachment, user identity, or DSN into either payload.

## Gateway and provisioning

The dependency-free gateway is `@odd-core/analytics/gateway` (ESM, Node 20+).
Run `node node_modules/@odd-core/analytics/gateway/server.mjs` in the private
deployment. Server-only configuration, supplied as mounted owner-only JSON files:

```json
// PROJECT_TOKENS_FILE
{"public-watcher-v1":{"app":"watcher","token":"PRIVATE_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN","features":["home","menu"]}}
// SENTRY_PROJECTS_FILE
{"public-watcher-cli-v1":{"app":"watcher","project_id":7,"public_key":"32_HEX_CHAR_PUBLIC_KEY","platform":"javascript","frames":["app:///main/index.js"]}}
```

Those aliases/IDs are examples, not provisioned projects. Maps route each alias
to a single backend project; caller-supplied project IDs, tokens, and properties
cannot select another tenant. Copy only public aliases into app configuration.
The server supports per-project `features`/`frames`; omitted lists preserve the
Hansel pilot defaults. The pilot gateway currently deployed in Hansel predates
these per-app lists: validate and deploy the shared gateway before using new
Watcher feature/source enums. Existing Hansel payloads remain compatible.

Optional `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is a JSON array of exact web origins; none by default.
Unlisted Origin headers are rejected. Permit OPTIONS for only the two intake
routes at ingress when enabling web apps; do not expose dashboard routes.
The process binds port 8080; provision private upstreams via `POSTHOG_UPSTREAM`
(default `http://proxy:80/batch/`) and `SENTRY_UPSTREAM` (`http://sentry-ingress`).
Standalone mode restricts upstream hostnames to the private service names/local
host; never configure a hosted provider fallback. Rate/body/connection limits
remain enabled. `GET /health` does not prove end-to-end ingestion.

Existing infrastructure runbooks and provisioning helpers are in
`/Users/exeai/Hansel/docs/analytics/`: `APP_SETUP.md`, `STATUS.md`, `SENTRY.md`,
`provision-hansel.py`, `provision-sentry.py`, `create-dashboard.py`,
`connect-sentry-intake.py`, and `backup/README.md`. Adapt scripts without replacing
Hansel mappings. Actual credentials stay on the server, outside source control.
Dashboards: PostHog `https://build-my.tail910c31.ts.net`, Sentry
`https://build-my.tail910c31.ts.net:8443` (Tailscale + Tailscale DNS).
Encrypted daily restic backups already use Cloudflare R2, seven-day retention.

## Checks and adoption status

`pnpm --filter @odd-core/analytics test` builds the package and runs the privacy,
wire-contract, project isolation, CORS, and gateway tests without live services.
`pnpm --filter @odd-core/analytics test:privacy` runs against an existing build.
The legacy API remains available; adding this entry point does not automatically
migrate apps, deploy the gateway, create projects, or qualify Swift/mobile builds.
Hansel's original integration has live dogfood evidence; this shared extraction
requires each consuming app's normal integration checks before rollout.

## Standard basic analytics (0.2.0)

Keep collection off until the person explicitly accepts a clear first-run choice.
Offer **Share Basic Analytics** and **Not Now**. An unchecked optional diagnostics
choice can share the same screen, while usage/errors remain independently
controllable in Settings. Persist a decline; never repeatedly prompt or silently
turn on a channel after an upgrade. Existing approved choices remain approved.
Apps must obtain their required platform/privacy permissions before collection.

The standard product dataset is consenting-installation DAU/WAU/MAU, foreground
active duration, real recording duration where applicable, allowlisted feature
counts/outcomes, numeric app version and coarse platform. `USAGE_DISCLOSURE` and
`DIAGNOSTICS_DISCLOSURE` provide shared field descriptions. Supply static
`appVersion: '1.0.48'` and `platform: 'macos'` to PrivacyClient; platform is one of
macos/windows/linux/ios/android/web. Neither field comes from arbitrary event data.
Feature results are `{ event: 'result', feature: 'menu', outcome: 'success' }`
(or `failure`), sent as app_result. No error text accompanies a failure counter.
The gateway independently validates metadata and results. Deploy that capability
before enabling result events in clients; old payloads remain compatible.

DAU/WAU/MAU use the same per-app random installation ID with UTC day/7-day/30-day
windows; no account or cross-app ID is necessary. Existing 30-day raw retention
limits the rolling monthly window. Counts cover consenting installations only.
